decisions.reason: Eliminating Big Block prizes and reallocating mint revenue does not change which NFT asset must be minted.
The FAQ still describes Big Block prizes and tickets and states a $4 founder share, all of which conflict with the new Small-Block-only $5/$5/$5 primary-mint allocation.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Joseph, id like to eliminate the big blocks and give that extra $1 to me, so it'll be:
$15 buy, $5 to me,  $5 to affiliate,  $5 to block prize pool.

Increases my bottom line with minimal impact on sales.
Plus it simplifies the game mechanics and marketing.

Giveing myself and each community member an even split, as well as everyone getting an even shot at the never ending $500 prizes seems aligned with the projects ethos.

value_updates.buyer_earnings: $5 instant referral commissions, Small Block prize tickets, and a possible future BooksOnChain governance token.
value_updates.prize_block_description: Small Block awards 5 × $500 about every 500 mint or secondary sales; its pool is funded from every sale. Big Block prizes are eliminated.
value_updates.prize_ticket_rules: Each successful coded referral earns one current Small Block ticket; more tickets provide more chances, and tickets expire after the Small Block is drawn.
value_updates.anti_scam_explanation: Explain that the model is single-level with verified source; on each $15 primary mint the client receives $5 minus applicable fiat fees, the affiliate receives $5, and $5 funds the Small Block prize pool.

decisions.reason: The revenue reallocation does not change the optional tipping control or its placement.
The source does not change the deferred Transak fiat-payment provider, flow, or supported payment methods.
The existing same-message Event records the $5 allocation but omits that the Small Block prize pool is now the only active funded prize pool.
